source_caption:
To heavily market the film, producer Dino De Laurentiis constantly boasted about a wildly expensive, 40-foot mechanical Kong. However, the multi-million-dollar animatronic was a complete disaster on set, leaking hydraulic fluid and barely functioning. Ultimately, it appears on screen for less than fifteen seconds. To actually save the movie, a deeply talented, young special effects artist named Rick Baker stepped in, wearing an incredibly hot, heavily modified ape suit he designed himself for almost every single shot. By abandoning the wildly expensive machine for a man in a handmade suit, the production masterfully proves that the most enduring cinematic magic often relies on raw, physical human performance rather than deeply unreliable, groundbreaking technology.
⠀
King Kong (1976), directed by John Guillermin, starring Jeff Bridges, Charles Grodin, Jessica Lange. A fiercely ambitious, deeply greedy oil executive and a fiercely compassionate primate paleontologist discover a massive, completely untamed giant ape on an uncharted island, bringing him back to a highly modernized New York City with profoundly devastating, tragically doomed results.

source_details.title: King Kong
source_details.synopsis: King Kong is a 1976 American adventure monster film, directed by John Guillermin. It is a remake of the 1933 film about a giant ape who is captured and taken to New York City for exhibition. It stars Jeff Bridges, Charles Grodin, and Jessica Lange, and features mechanical effects by Carlo Rambaldi and makeup effects by Rick Baker, who also portrayed King Kong. It is the fifth entry in the King Kong franchise. The idea to remake King Kong was conceived in 1974 by Michael Eisner, who was then an ABC executive.
